description: ASML Holding N.V. is a Dutch multinational public corporation headquartered in Veldhoven, Netherlands, that develops and manufactures photolithography machines for the semiconductor industry. It is the world's leading lithography tool manufacturer with over 90% market share and the sole producer of extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems essential for advanced microchip production. ASML operates in more than 60 locations worldwide, with major hubs in Veldhoven (Netherlands), Silicon Valley (USA), Wilton (USA), and across Asia. The company employs over 44,000 people representing more than 100 nationalities. ASML's revenue is globally diversified: Taiwan (24.7%), China (22.2%), South Korea (21.3%), United States (9.6%), EMEA (3.7%), Japan (1.9%), and Singapore (0.9%). The company is listed on Euronext Amsterdam and NASDAQ under the ticker ASML, with a market capitalization of approximately €539.5 billion as of early 2026.

revenueGeography.reason: Extracted ASML revenue geography from the most recent available data. The latest full fiscal year is 2025 (total net sales €32.7B per ASML Q4 2025 press release and Wikipedia). The most detailed geographic breakdown comes from AlphaSpread data showing 2025 revenue of €32.7B with regional splits: Taiwan 24.7%, China 22.2%, South Korea 21.3%, United States 9.6%, EMEA 3.7%, Japan 1.9%, Singapore 0.9%, Netherlands 0.1%, Rest of Asia 0%. Additional context from ECIPE (2023: China 26.3%, Taiwan 29.3%) and ASML press release (2025 China ~20% of total net sales) corroborates the directional trends. The AlphaSpread data is the most granular and consistent with the €32.7B total for FY2025.

revenueGeography.concentrationRisk: ASML has significant geographic concentration risk with Taiwan (24.7%), China (22.2%), and South Korea (21.3%) collectively accounting for approximately 68% of total revenue. The company is heavily reliant on the Asia-Pacific region. Export control risks are particularly notable for China exposure, with US and Dutch export restrictions expected to impact China sales. ASML expects China business to be around 20% of total net sales for 2025, down from 26.3% in 2023.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: US Export Controls on EUV/DUV Lithography
geopoliticalRisks.description: US export controls restrict ASML's sale of advanced EUV and DUV lithography machines to China. The October 2023 US rules impose a '0% de minimis' rule capturing all ASML equipment destined for China. The December 2024 update expanded restrictions to include metrology and software, and added Chinese fab locations. ASML's China business represents ~20% of total revenue.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Dutch Government Export Controls Aligned with US
geopoliticalRisks.description: The Dutch government imposed national export controls on ASML in September 2023, January 2024, and September 2024, restricting shipments of DUV immersion lithography systems to China. In January 2025, ASML was required to apply for export licenses with the Dutch government instead of the US. These controls directly impact ASML's primary revenue stream.

The MATCH Act (Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware), proposed in April 2026, would prohibit new equipment sales to China AND servicing/maintenance of previously sold machines. It enforces a 150-day deadline for allies like the Netherlands to conform or face sanctions. Could cost ASML ~17% of revenue based on quarterly sales drop to China.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Taiwan Strait Conflict Risk to Supply Chain
geopoliticalRisks.description: Taiwan is the world's most important silicon chokepoint with TSMC holding ~90% of advanced AI chip market share. A China-Taiwan conflict would disrupt the global semiconductor supply chain, severely impacting ASML's customers and demand for lithography equipment. New fab construction lead times are now 3-5 years.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: IP Theft and Technology Leakage to China
geopoliticalRisks.description: ASML reported a former employee allegedly stole information about company technology and went to work for Huawei. China secretly built a prototype EUV machine in Shenzhen with assistance from former ASML engineers. Dongfang Jingyuan Electron Limited was marketing products potentially infringing ASML's IP rights.

The September 2025 update of EU Annex I added semiconductor manufacturing equipment to the EU control list. The European Commission noted 'the lack of a common EU voice exposes individual Member States to geopolitical pressures' referencing ASML. EU-produced items from the Netherlands continue to be found in Russian military equipment despite sanctions.

The Trump administration launched an investigation into national security risks of imported semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act. In January 2026, a 25% tariff on semiconductors was imposed with case-by-case review for H200 chips to China.

In January 2023, the US, Netherlands, and Japan (controlling ~90% of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment) agreed to jointly restrict China's access to frontier chip-making tools. The agreement includes no allied backfilling of US-restricted equipment to China and technology thresholds aligned with US controls.

China is actively developing domestic chipmaking technology, including a prototype EUV machine in Shenzhen built with former ASML engineers. China's Phase II National IC Industry Investment Fund ($28.9-47B) focuses on semiconductor equipment. Export restrictions may force China to accelerate domestic alternatives, creating future competition for ASML.

ASML incorporates US technology in equipment design, making it subject to US export regulations under the FDPR. The December 2024 update created new FDPRs and updated de minimis provisions expanding unilateral US authority, potentially capturing all semiconductor manufacturing equipment made globally. The '0% de minimis' rule extends US jurisdiction regardless of actual US content.

BIS created ECCN 3B090 covering semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related items, directly affecting ASML's lithography machine exports. The October 2023 BIS update expanded criteria for restricted items and extended geographic scope to 43 more countries with AI ties to China.

In December 2023, the Netherlands' Institute for Human Rights ruled ASML could reject job applications from residents of countries subject to US sanctions (China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria), impacting talent acquisition and operations.

ASML cited increasing uncertainty driven by macro-economic and geopolitical developments affecting 2026 outlook. CEO stated that 2026 guidance bandwidth accommodates potential outcomes of ongoing discussions around export controls. Eurozone GDP growth forecast revised down to 0.7% for 2026.

The Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) prohibits US persons from engaging in certain transactions involving advanced semiconductors with China, including Hong Kong and Macau, further constraining the ecosystem in which ASML's customers operate.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: US CHIPS Act Subsidies Distorting Competition
geopoliticalRisks.description: The US CHIPS and Science Act set aside nearly $50 billion to grow US semiconductor manufacturing capacity. South Korea, Japan, India, and the EU have announced similar measures. These subsidies could shift demand away from ASML's export-dependent model toward regionalized production.
